correctness.rationale: For each positive radius \(r\), every full-column interval has at most \(2r-1\) columns and all off-interval tips lie in the source row. The endpoint-overlap charging argument gives a bound on tip redundancy: \(\sum_x((a_x-1)_++(b_x-1)_+)\le\sum_p(M_p-1)\). Every unfilled column costs one overlap unit when \(m\ge4\), whereas for \(m=3\) at most one hole can use the sole radius-zero source without such a cost. Hence the exact upper cutoffs \((k-1)^2\) and \((k-1)^2+1\), plus a separate two-round exclusion for \(n>1\). Explicit interval tilings and a three-row gap construction attain the bounds. Clamping sources proves shorter paths. The standalone Python verifier checked 236 constructions, 30 exact instances, and 891 endpoint-budget instances; finite tests are supplementary.

evidence: Mitsche–Prałat–Roshanbin (2018), Theorem 7: for connected graphs, \(\max\{b(G),b(H)\}\le b(G\boxtimes H)\le b(G\square H)\le\min\{b(G)+\operatorname{rad}(H),b(H)+\operatorname{rad}(G)\}\); for a clique and path this gives \(\lceil\sqrt n\rceil\le b\le\lceil\sqrt n\rceil+1\).
Their next paragraph explicitly says the upper bound is attained for arbitrary radius-one factor when the path has square order.
Antony et al. (2024), Sections 3–5, treat proper interval-graph hardness, P_k-free upper bounds, edge/total burning.
broader_coverage.reasoning: None of these stronger-general-scope published results supplies equality for all nonsquare n or establishes a jump specific to K_3. The known square-order subcase is subsumed; it is not part of claimed new mathematical content.

value.rationale: Completes the ordinary burning number for every Cartesian clique–path product with at least three clique vertices and every path order. The exact sharp horizon boundary gives a qualitative transition: width three gains one extra column via three source tips, while every width at least four has a squared-interval cutoff. This closes nonsquare cases left undecided by general graph-product bounds and isolates a reusable geometric obstruction; the result does not claim the known square-order or ladder cases as new.
